Revised assessment: The ongoing public health crisis will continue to weigh on activity, employment, and inflation; however, the FOMC’s adoption of average inflation targeting (a “makeup” strategy) and its continued Treasury and agency MBS purchases, together with repo and ON RRP operations, constitute forward guidance and QE tools that the macro-finance literature finds effective at the zero lower bound in lowering term premiums, anchoring inflation expectations, and supporting real activity. COVID-19 elevated economic policy uncertainty and generated demand and supply-chain shocks, while lower oil prices damped inflation pressures, consistent with a subdued near-term Phillips curve response; yet the policy backstop materially mitigates downside risks relative to the initial shock.
